subject: ela
intro: Students identify who is telling a story at various points in a text, distinguishing between a first-person narrator (uses 'I') and a third-person narrator (uses 'he,' 'she,' 'they,' or the character's name). Students also recognize when different characters are speaking within a story.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

I walked to school on a cold morning. I could see my breath in the air. I found a shiny penny on the sidewalk and put it in my pocket.

Who is telling this story? How do you know?

steps: I look for clue words: who is speaking in this story?
I see the word 'I' used many times: 'I walked,' 'I could see,' 'I found.'
When a narrator uses 'I,' it means they are telling their own story.
This is called a first-person narrator.
solution.answer: The narrator is telling their own story. We know because the word 'I' is used throughout. This is a first-person narrator.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Maya walked to school on a cold morning. She could see her breath in the air. She found a shiny penny on the sidewalk and put it in her pocket.

Who is telling this story? How does this version differ from the first one?

steps: I look for clue words.
The story uses 'Maya,' 'she,' and 'her' instead of 'I.'
When the narrator talks about the character using their name or 'he/she/they,' the narrator is outside the story.
This is called a third-person narrator.
It differs from the first version because we do not feel like we are inside Maya's head as much.
solution.answer: Someone outside the story is telling it. The narrator uses Maya's name and the word 'she.' This is a third-person narrator. In the first version, the narrator was a character in the story using 'I.'

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sam ran to the tree. 'I found it!' he shouted. 'What did you find?' asked Leo.

Who is telling the story? Who is speaking in the quotations?

steps: The main narration says 'Sam ran' and 'he shouted.' This is third-person narration.
Inside the quotation marks, Sam speaks in first-person: 'I found it!'
Leo also speaks inside quotation marks: 'What did you find?'
The narrator is third-person, but the characters speak in first-person inside quotation marks.
solution.answer: The narrator is a third-person narrator (using 'Sam' and 'he'). Inside the story, Sam speaks using 'I,' and Leo also speaks. When characters talk, their speech appears in quotation marks.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

I am Biscuit the dog. My owner is Aisha. Every morning, I wag my tail when she wakes up. I love mornings best.

Who is the narrator of this story? What is special about this narrator?

steps: The narrator uses 'I' and says 'I am Biscuit the dog.'
So the narrator is a dog named Biscuit.
This is a first-person narrator, but it is an animal narrator.
This is unusual because animals cannot really talk or tell stories.
solution.answer: The narrator is Biscuit the dog. This is a first-person narrator (uses 'I'). What is special is that the narrator is an animal, which is a creative choice by the author to give us the dog's point of view.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

Zoe was reading quietly when Ben ran in. 'The cat is stuck!' he yelled. Zoe jumped up. 'Where?' she asked. 'In the big oak tree,' Ben answered.

Who is telling the story? Which characters speak, and how do you know when they are speaking?

steps: The main narrator uses Zoe's and Ben's names and words like 'she' and 'he.' Third-person narrator.
Characters who speak have their words in quotation marks.
Ben says: 'The cat is stuck!' and 'In the big oak tree.'
Zoe says: 'Where?'
Quotation marks tell us when a character is speaking.
solution.answer: A third-person narrator tells the story using names and 'she/he.' Ben and Zoe both speak. We know they are speaking because their words appear inside quotation marks.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

I love rainy days. I put on my boots and jump in every puddle I can find. My dog Marco runs with me and barks at the rain.

Is the narrator first-person or third-person? How do you know?
items.hint: Look for the word 'I' or for character names and 'he/she.'

steps: The story uses 'I' and 'My' throughout.
The narrator is speaking about themselves.
This is a first-person narrator.
solution.answer: The narrator is first-person. We know because the story uses 'I love,' 'I put on,' and 'My dog.' The narrator is telling their own story.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

Leo woke up early on his birthday. He ran to the kitchen. His family was already there with a cake. 'Happy birthday!' they shouted.

Who is telling this story? Which characters speak?
items.hint: Look for 'I' or for names like 'Leo' and pronouns like 'he.'

steps: The narrator uses 'Leo,' 'He,' and 'His,' not 'I.'
This is a third-person narrator.
Leo's family speaks: 'Happy birthday!'
Their speech is in quotation marks.
solution.answer: A third-person narrator tells the story using 'Leo' and 'he.' Leo's family speaks when they say 'Happy birthday!' Their words are in quotation marks.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

I am a little red hen. I found some wheat in the field one day. 'Who will help me plant this wheat?' I asked. 'Not I!' said the duck. 'Not I!' said the cat.

Who is the narrator? Who speaks in this story? How can you tell the difference between when the narrator speaks and when characters speak?
items.hint: Look for 'I' in the narration and look for quotation marks when characters speak.

steps: The narrator is the little red hen. She uses 'I am a little red hen' and 'I found.'
The narrator also speaks in quotation marks: 'Who will help me plant this wheat?'
The duck and cat speak in quotation marks: 'Not I!'
Quotation marks show when characters speak. The narration outside the quotes is the hen telling her own story.
solution.answer: The narrator is the little red hen, who tells the story in first-person using 'I.' The duck and cat are characters who speak inside quotation marks. The hen also speaks inside quotation marks at one point. The narration outside quotation marks is the hen's storytelling voice.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

Aisha opened the box carefully. Marco leaned in to see. 'What is it?' he asked. Aisha smiled. 'A puppy,' she whispered.

Count the number of different characters who speak. Who is the narrator?
items.hint: Look for quotation marks to find the speakers. Look for 'he/she/they' to find the narrator.

steps: Character 1: Marco speaks: 'What is it?'
Character 2: Aisha speaks: 'A puppy.'
Two characters speak.
The narrator uses 'Aisha,' 'Marco,' 'he,' and 'she.' This is third-person narration.
solution.answer: Two characters speak: Marco and Aisha. Their words are in quotation marks. The narrator is a third-person narrator who uses the characters' names and the words 'he' and 'she.'

items.prompt:
Read this story below. At first, one narrator is telling the story. Then a different character takes over. Notice when the narrator changes.

I like to read stories to my little sister. She always asks for more.

'Tell me one more,' she begged.
'It is bedtime,' I said.
'Please!' she said again.

How many different people speak in this story? Is the main narrator first-person or third-person?
items.hint: Check who uses 'I' and whose words are in quotation marks.

steps: The main narrator uses 'I' at the start: 'I like to read.' First-person narrator.
Inside the story, two characters speak: the sister ('Tell me one more' and 'Please!') and the narrator ('It is bedtime').
So two people speak: the narrator and the little sister.
The main narrator is first-person.
solution.answer: Two people speak: the narrator and the little sister. The main narrator is first-person (uses 'I'). In the dialogue, both the narrator and the sister speak inside quotation marks.
